frontier.hypothesis: loop.c's elimination of the stptr biv — residual (b), and the thing that makes the honest real-loop chassis cost bytes — can be blocked by giving stptr a use that loop.c cannot reduce to a giv, and blocking it re-lays the entire priority landscape (stptr returns as an allocno, pseudo 125 stops consuming a seat), which may also dissolve residual (a).
frontier.mechanism: loop.c's maybe_eliminate_biv only eliminates a biv when every use of it is either the exit comparison or a giv. In loop1, stptr's only uses are `stptr + 0x38` and `*(s16 *)(stptr + 6)` — both givs — plus the increment, so it is fully reducible. A use of the RAW value that survives the loop makes bl->all_reduced false and the biv stays.
frontier.next_probe: Exploit E-s26-11: stptr at loop1 exit and stptr2 at loop2 entry are the same value (base+0x7E4). Measure forms where loop1's stptr is live after the loop — starting with `stptr2 = stptr;` (which deletes `saved` and its 0x18($sp) spill, so expect an insn shortfall, but read the allocno table and the loop1 body FIRST to see whether the giv dies) and then forms that keep `saved`/the spill for the block-2 bytes while still giving stptr a surviving raw use. Require in ONE measurement: no `addu $19,$2,308`/`sh $8,-50($19)` in the loop1 body AND build_insns == 132.
